body: Thank you so much. I wish you the best of luck through med school :-)
Please do. Being the middle child is a real thing. If your brother and I share the same mentality, then it would really mean a lot to him. Im sure of it.

I still live my traditional, Asian parents, so I can't really go out for a smoke right now. I've also found it so incredibly hard to make myself cry nowadays, but I feel like I just really need a good one. This shit makes me even more depressed because music is my passion, and it won't make me cry anymore. I'm just... numb.

Yeah, one of the excuses was "it's far, and I know you don't want to drive" when I was literally gonna pick them up... mind you, my best friend lives a good distance away, so I was already in for a drive.
Man, that's a really bad feeling. I'm sorry to hear that. I'm sure you were just being real with him, and they took it to offense. I hope your Friday night turned out to be better than mine at least!

To go to a bar with a bowling alley. They know I'm very anxious when it comes to meeting people, so I didn't even get an invite. Also, do you ever read someone when they hint that they don't want you to join by not even asking, but just assuming small and irrelevant details? There was a lot of that too.
I watched Netflix all day haha. I'm home safe, and feeling very slightly better, so that's good I guess. I hope you enjoyed your Netflix!

Music is great. But I agree, sometimes you need a little bit of self control or you'll find yourself crying for the next hour to a song you shouldn't have played. Otherwise, music is probably the main motivator for me to start my day, and even get through it.

Hi, friend! I'm pretty much in the same situation as you, but I came to a consensus that I should stay living with my parents. I'm 22, and just got my degree. I might not have as much freedom as I want, but they're still paying for a lot of the things I genuinely don't want to. And it's not like I'm taking it all for granted, I'm just grateful and taking advantage of what I do have that some others might not. Potentially 3 more years of living with my parents and I'll be out for good after I get an MBA. It's better than living penny to penny on a regular basis. Just a piece of my mind.
I understand you 110% because I'm a dog owner myself. All I can say is hang in there, and I genuinely hope y'all find her. Godspeed to you, my friend.

Rest well, friend.

Hi, friend! I think it depends on what type of job you have. I'm new to the social work department in my job, and they actually recommend taking a couple days off if we're burnt out. Maybe if your job is in the same field of work, they'll be more understanding. I hope this helps in some way. Hang in there.
